newsitem.title: USA: U.S. EPA seeks to allow 30 new areas use RFG.
newsitem.headline: U.S. EPA seeks to allow 30 new areas use RFG.

text.p: The White House is reviewing a proposal by the Environmental Protection Agency to let about 30 more areas in the United States use reformulated gasoline (RFG) to help control smog, EPA officials said Tuesday.
The plan would allow areas which formerly failed to meet federal ozone standards but no longer have serious smog problems to require use of reformulated gasoline to help them stay out of trouble.
The White House Office of Management and Budget must approve the plan by late December before the EPA may issue a formal proposal for public comment, an EPA official said.
The earliest a rule could be issued after going through a public comment process would be next summer, she said.
"We don't know how many areas are interested. Some have said they want it for maintenance," she said.
Under the Clean Air Act, areas which had extremely smoggy air were required to use RFG, and areas with serious pollution problems were allowed to opt into the RFG program.
Areas which would fall under the new proposal include Kansas City, Raleigh-Durham, Indianapolis, Miami, Memphis, Detroit, San Francisco, Tampa-St. Petersburg, and several cities in Ohio.
